one_month_reasoning: No Dycom earnings fall inside 2026-10-09 to 2026-11-08: Dycom's fiscal Q3 (quarter ending 2026-10-31) is reported in late November (the prior-year Q3 print moved the stock in the week of 2025-11-17), so after the window. Inside the window are value-chain read-throughs only: AT&T and Verizon Q3 (late Oct; fiber build pace and capex), Corning Q3 (late Oct; carrier vs enterprise optical demand), MasTec and Quanta Q3 (late Oct/early Nov; MasTec's communications outlook was cut in July, so another cut is a modest negative risk, stabilisation a modest positive), Lumen Q3 (early Nov) and hyperscaler Q3 capex updates (late Oct; 2026 guides were raised in July). These move DY a few percent each but are not decisive. Short-horizon regularities pull both ways: strong negative price momentum (down ~52% from the May high, 52-week low set in the last fortnight) versus oversold reversal and a 14.6x forward P/E against 20-24x for peers. Net: I stay close to symmetric around $269 with monthly sigma ~14.5% (52% annual / 3.5), median ~$270, no directional tilt.

fair_value.method: Blend of 16x NTM EPS at Oct-2027 (~$21.45, i.e. FY28 consensus $20.78 haircut 4% then rolled 3 quarters forward at 10%) = $343 (60%) and 11x FY28E EBITDA $1.20B less ~$2.18B net debt over 30.16M shares = $365 (40%); blended ~$352.

inputs_detail.derivation: StockAnalysis 'EPS Next Year' 20.78; FY2027 table average 17.05.

Communications is ~80% of DY revenue (Q2: $1,608.4M of $2,005.9M). Peer MasTec's communications EBITDA margin fell 170bp to 8.2% and its communications 18-month backlog slipped QoQ ($5,501M -> $5,461M); DY itself guided Communications margin down slightly and deferred ~$150M wireless revenue. I trim consensus ~4% (~ a 50bp Communications margin miss on ~$6.5B FY28 Communications revenue, after tax, over ~30M shares) to reflect that chain-wide softness.

$19.95 x (1 + 10% x 0.75 yr). 10% FY29 growth is below FY28 consensus revenue growth (+13.2%, src 3), supported by multi-year carrier build targets (FBA 11.8M homes passed in 2025 and ~60M first-time passings remaining; Verizon 40-50M passings medium term; AT&T 60M fiber locations by 2030).

Peer forward P/E median 23.65x, range 15.75x (LMB) to 38.32x (PWR); DY trades at 14.6x. 16x sits inside the range near the low end, slightly above DY's current multiple, and below MTZ (19.89x), the closest telecom comparable; the discount to the median is argued in comps_summary (customer concentration, weak H1 cash conversion, leverage, telecom end-market softness).

bear.story: The telecom chain keeps softening: wireless deferrals spread, carriers slow fiber builds after the AT&T/Lumen and Verizon/Frontier deals close, BEAD stays slow, and an AI-capex pause hits long-haul/inside-the-fence fiber. FY28 EPS resets to ~$16 and the stock trades at ~12x, a de-rated multiple on a leveraged balance sheet with weak cash conversion.

base.story: FY27 is delivered (revenue $7.48-7.66B), FY28 EPS ~$20 (consensus less a small chain-wide haircut), and estimates hold. The multiple recovers only partly, to ~14-15x, because the telecom end-market stays mixed (MasTec communications softness) while momentum fades. Partial convergence toward fair value of ~$350.

bull.story: The $12.2B backlog converts and the deferred $150M wireless work lands in FY28. Hyperscaler capex keeps rising in 2027 (2026 guides were already raised) and data-center fiber plus Power Solutions drive beats. The multiple re-rates toward ~20x (MasTec level) on ~$22 NTM EPS.

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E 15.75x (LMB) to 38.32x (PWR); trailing EV/EBITDA 11.0x (LMB) to 36.9x (PWR). Forward EV/EBITDA is not available from the source, so the EV/EBITDA median and range are trailing.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 16.0x NTM P/E against a 23.65x median: inside the range, near the low end (LMB 15.75x), below MasTec 19.89x, and slightly above DY's own 14.6x. 11.0x next-year EV/EBITDA against a 17.3x trailing median sits at the bottom of the range.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: A discount to the median should persist through the horizon for evidenced, structural reasons. (1) Customer concentration: AT&T 20.1%, Verizon 10.4% and Lumen 5.3% made up 35.8% of Q2 revenue (10-Q), against the diversified utility/commercial bases of EME, FIX and PWR. (2) Cash conversion: H1 FY27 operating cash flow of $79.1M was below capex of $139.8M. (3) Leverage: net debt ~$2.48B, about 2.3x estimated FY27 EBITDA of ~$1.07B (H1 $578.0M + Q3 guide midpoint $291.5M + ~ $200M estimated for Q4), after the $2.0B Power Solutions deal, whereas EME, FIX, STRL, IESC and AGX have net cash per their EV < market cap. (4) The telecom end-market is softening across the chain: MasTec communications margins fell 170bp, its communications backlog slipped QoQ, and both MasTec and DY flagged wireless slowdowns. I do not go below the peer range, because DY's FY28 EPS growth (+22%) matches the peer median and its Building Systems segment (24.5% Q2 EBITDA margin) is a data-center business that peers EME and FIX show the market pays 23-32x for.

thesis_break_reason: $195 is ~27% below the current price and ~9.4x FY28 consensus EPS. A trade there would mean the market has reset FY28 EPS to the low-to-mid teens: a major-customer capex cut (AT&T or Verizon, together ~30% of revenue), a broad wireline deferral like MasTec's turning into cancellations, an AI-capex digestion that hits data-center fiber and Power Solutions, or a covenant or cash-flow problem given ~$2.5B of net debt and negative H1 FCF. Ordinary volatility is unlikely to explain it.

reasoning: Facts: DY fell from $566 (May) to $269, mostly after the Aug 26 Q2 FY27 print. That quarter beat (revenue $2.006B +45.6%, organic +16.7%, adj. EPS $5.29, backlog $12.24B +53%), but the Q3 guide midpoint ($4.56 EPS, $291.5M EBITDA) came in under consensus and ~$150M of wireless revenue slipped to FY28. Price targets were cut (src 5/6), yet consensus EPS stands at FY27 $17.05 and FY28 $20.78 (src 3), so the stock now trades at 14.6x forward vs a 23.65x peer median. Industry lane: the chain is mixed. Negatives: MasTec, the closest competitor, cut its communications outlook in July (margin -170bp to 8.2%, comm backlog down QoQ), corroborating a telecom/wireless lull. Positives: carrier fiber targets remain large (FBA: record 11.8M homes passed in 2025 with ~60M first-time passings left; Verizon 2M new passings in 2026 and 40-50M medium term; AT&T 60M by 2030), and hyperscalers raised 2026 capex (Alphabet $195-205B, Amazon ~$220B, Meta $130-145B, Microsoft ~$175B CY26). Lumen's Q2 showed strategic revenue +14% but nothing on build pace. Valuation: 16x NTM EPS and 11x FY28 EBITDA, both at the low end of an 11-peer range because of concentration, leverage and cash conversion, give ~$352 fair value. The distribution is a three-scenario lognormal mixture (bear $195 / 30%, base $305 / 45%, bull $440 / 25%; median ~$299, mean ~$316, log-sd ~0.40), with the left tail widened toward the stock's 52% realized vol. Valuation support and rising estimates are offset by severe negative momentum and real chain softness, so P(>= $269) is ~0.60, not higher. The 1-month view is near-neutral because DY's own Q3 report falls just after the window. Research limits: Twelve Data/Alpha Vantage statistics endpoints were paywalled; MasTec's segment guidance page, Corning's release, the Lumen deck and AT&T's release could not be opened (403/402/binary), so their figures are not used; forward EV/EBITDA for peers was unavailable, so trailing is shown.
